# meteobr

The goal of `meteobr` is to provide an easy way to get data from the
automated meteorological stations of Brazil’s [National Institute of
Meteorology](https://portal.inmet.gov.br/). These stations provide, at
each hour of every day between 2000-2024, a plethora of useful data (see
the vignette [data
trivia](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/articles/data_trivia.html)).

## Installation

You can install the development version of meteobr from
[GitHub](https://github.com/carlosdemoura/meteobr/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("carlosdemoura/meteobr")
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

``` r

library(meteobr)

get_data(first.day = "2001-01-01", last.day = "2001-01-02")
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`get_data()`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/get_data.md)
  : Get meteorological data within interval
- [`get_inmet_data_by_year()`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/get_inmet_data_by_year.md)
  : Get data from INMET website
- [`info_repo`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/info_repo.md)
  : Informations about data file
- [`local_data()`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/local_data.md)
  : Get where data is stored
- [`meteobr.max.year`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/meteobr.max.year.md)
  : Package maximum yaer available
- [`set_data_locally()`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/set_data_locally.md)
  : Download preprocessed data
- [`stations`](https://carlosdemoura.github.io/meteobr/reference/stations.md)
  : Additional information about INMET's automatic stations
